vocab.title: Match each expression to its meaning
defs: extra information that makes something clearer
a case that is allowed even when the rule says no
to say no to a request, in a formal and polite way
at this point of the process, and possibly not later
the set of rules used to decide between yes and no
the final approval of a person with authority

reading.rtitle: Yes, No and Not Yet, in Writing
paras: A request arrives from a manager: he wants to open a new position. The business reason is real, the budget situation is difficult, and the answer has to leave the relationship intact. In English, three answers are possible, and they are not simply yes, no and maybe.

The first one is the yes with a condition. "The replacement is approved, subject to approval by the CFO." Nothing here is vague: the decision is positive, the next step has an owner, and the manager knows that one more sign-off is missing. A yes without that last line creates a promise that HR cannot keep.

The second one is the not yet, and it is the most useful of the three. "Could you provide more details about the workload and the monthly cost?" The request is not refused; it is incomplete. The manager receives a task instead of a refusal, and the decision moves forward without anybody losing the argument.

The third one is the no. "I'm afraid we can't approve a new position at this stage." Two expressions do the work. I'm afraid announces bad news politely, and at this stage says that the door is closed today and not forever. After that, one reason, and then one date: in January we look at the position again.

The three answers share the same shape: the decision first, then one reason, then one next step with a date. What changes is the level of firmness, not the level of politeness. A no with a reason is easier to accept than a yes nobody can confirm.
reading.source: Alumni by Better -- model replies written for this lesson; no real request or employee data is used

gist.prompt: What do the three answers have in common?
choices: They all avoid giving a clear decision, so that nobody is disappointed.
Each one gives the decision, one reason and one next step with a date.
They all leave the final decision to the manager who made the request.

items: A yes should always say if another sign-off is still missing.
'A yes without that last line creates a promise that HR cannot keep.'
The text says the not yet is the least useful of the three answers.
The opposite: 'it is the most useful of the three'.
"At this stage" means the request will never be approved.
It 'says that the door is closed today and not forever'.
In the not yet, the manager receives something to do.
'The manager receives a task instead of a refusal.'
According to the text, what changes between the three answers is how polite they are.
'What changes is the level of firmness, not the level of politeness.'

items.situation: A manager asks for a new position this quarter. The answer is no.
tips: I'm afraid we can't approve a new position at this stage.
I AM afraid. Never I have afraid.

items.situation: The request is incomplete: you need the cost and the workload.
tips: Could you provide more details about the workload and the monthly cost?

items.situation: The replacement is fine, but the CFO still has to sign.
tips: The replacement is approved, subject to approval by the CFO.
Say who still has to sign.

items.situation: He asks why his case is not an exception.
tips: The criteria for an exception are a critical role and a cost inside the budget.
Name the criteria, not your opinion.

items.situation: He wants to make an offer before the budget is confirmed.
tips: Let us hold off on the offer until the budget is confirmed.

items.situation: He asks when he can ask again.
tips: We look at the position again in January.

listenings.text: Camila, hello, it's the manager of the credit team. I sent you a request this morning and I want to explain it, because it is not a replacement. It is a new position, and I know the situation this quarter. Here is my justification. In March my team took on the Chile portfolio, and since then the volume of files has grown by about a third. Nobody left, so on paper nothing changed, but in practice one analyst is doing the work of two people. I am not asking for three positions. I am asking for one, and I am asking now because if I wait for January, I lose the two good candidates I have. Please tell me what you need from me and I prepare it today.

Good morning, this is a short message from finance about approvals this quarter. The rule has not changed: new positions are on hold until January. Replacements are still possible, and exceptions exist, but only with two criteria together. First, the role has to be critical, which means the business stops or a legal obligation is not met without it. Second, the cost has to be inside the budget we already approved for the year. If one of the two is missing, the answer is no, and it is better for everybody to hear that in the first week than in the fourth. One request to HR: send me the business justification in three lines and the monthly cost. Three lines are enough. Thank you.
